questions.prompt: In Newmarket, a dog off the owner’s property is not “at large” if it is on a retractable leash no longer than:
questions.excerpt:
Footnotes: --- ( 1 ) --- State Law reference— Animals, RSA 466—470.

Footnotes: --- ( 2 ) --- State Law reference— Dogs and cats, RSA 466.

The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the
               meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates
               a different meaning: At large means off the premises or property of the owner while not on a fixed leash of eight
               feet or less or a retractable leash of 15 feet or less, not under the physical control
               of a responsible person, and/or not confined within a vehicle. Dog includes both male and female of the canine species. The term "dog" shall also mean
               any animal, which is considered to be a wolf-hybrid as defined in RSA 466-A. Enclosure means any structure, fenced or otherwise, which is secure on all sides so as to prevent
               the exiting of the dog or entrance of young children. Said enclosure shall be of a
               proper size as regulated by state law. Enforcement official means any animal control officer, police officer, or other individual authorized
               to enforce the provisions of this article and such state statutes pertaining to animals. Owner means any person, group, association or organization responsible for maintaining,
               keeping, caring for, harboring or owning a dog. Threatening means an indication of a dog's imminent attack, usually accompanied by the baring
               of teeth and the fur on its back standing up. (Guttural threatening sounds made by
               an angry animal; low guttural menacing sound of a dog; a deep, angry, throaty noise
               as of a dog.) Vicious dog. (1) The term "vicious dog" means any dog which snaps at, bites or chases any person while
                  on foot or on any propelled vehicle. It shall also include any dog which has attacked
                  any animal, as domestic or wild.…
